Name: Dark Descent - Immersive Mines and Dungeon Darkness
Author: AnnaCharles
Description:
[center][b][size=6]Dark Descent[/size][/b][/center]
[center][i]Immersive Mine and Dungeon Darkness[/i][/center]
[center][i]The underground is dark again.[/i][/center]

[center]Dark Descent makes Stardew Valley’s Mines and dungeons dynamically darker, with different levels of darkness each time you descend.[/center]
[center]Some floors are dim. Some are dark. Some leave you relying heavily on whatever light you brought with you.[/center]

[center]Built-in dungeon lights can also fail, leaving only occasional pools of light in the darkness while Torches, Glow Rings, lava, and other genuine light sources still shine through.[/center]

[center]No fake black overlay. No permanent pitch-black caves. Just darker, more atmospheric underground exploration where light actually matters.[/center]

[center][youtube]hGaBDwUCFWk[/youtube][/center]
[center]
[color=#f1c232][size=1][font=Verdana][b]A little support goes a long way.[/b][/font][/size][/color]
[color=#f1c232][size=1][font=Verdana][b] Endorsements, comments, and feedback help these mods grow and inspire what comes next.[/b][/font][/size][/color]
[color=#f1c232][size=1][font=Verdana][b] Thanks for being part of it.[/b][/font][/size][/color][/center]



[b]🌑 DYNAMIC DUNGEON DARKNESS[/b]
Dark Descent adds additional darkness to supported underground areas while preserving real local light sources.
Every floor can fall into a different darkness level:
• Breather - lighter, but still noticeably darker than normal.
• Dim - atmospheric darkness with reduced visibility.
• Dark - personal light becomes much more valuable.
• Deep Dark - some unlit areas can become extremely difficult to see.
The result is intentionally varied.
One floor might give you some breathing room.
The next might make you very glad you brought a Torch.


[b]🔥 PERFECT WITH FADING TORCHES[/b]
Dark Descent is an especially good match for our other mod:
Fading Torches
Fading Torches gives Stardew Valley’s Torches a real lifecycle. Placed Torches slowly burn down, lose brightness and eventually go out, while portable Torchlight lets you sacrifice a Torch for temporary light that follows your farmer.
Together:
• darker caves make Torches genuinely useful.
• portable Torchlight becomes much more valuable underground.
• failing dungeon lights make carrying your own light worth considering.
• fading Torches make longer underground trips feel more atmospheric.
• surviving pools of dungeon light become meaningful places to catch your breath.
Dark Descent handles the darkness.
Fading Torches gives you the light.
Neither mod requires the other.


[b]🌓 LIGHTS CAN FAIL[/b]
Darkness is only half of Dark Descent.
With the Light Failure System enabled, ordinary environmental dungeon lights can fail too.
Wall lamps, braziers, sconces, and similar decorative lighting may simply not be working when you arrive.
This creates isolated pockets of light instead of rooms filled with overlapping illumination.
In darker places such as Skull Cavern and Quarry Mine, most rooms may have only one working ordinary light source — or none at all.
Large rooms can occasionally have more, but naturally bright dungeon rooms are intentionally uncommon.
Dark Descent protects lighting that is important for gameplay, including things such as:
• important navigation and exits
• required ladders and interactions
• quest or puzzle lighting
• important hazards
• Volcano lava and identity-critical lighting
• player-controlled light sources
Darkness should make exploration more atmospheric - not make required progression unknowable.


[b]🔦 YOUR LIGHT STILL MATTERS[/b]
Dark Descent does not simply cover the screen with darkness.
Real light still cuts through it.
That includes things such as:
• Torches
• Glow Rings
• farmer-attached light
• portable light sources
• surviving dungeon lamps
• Volcano lava and other protected authored lighting
The darker the floor, the more noticeable those light sources become.
Walking into a Deep Dark floor with your own Torch feels very different from entering empty-handed.


[b]⛏️ SUPPORTED DUNGEONS[/b]
Dark Descent currently supports:
• The Mines
• Skull Cavern
• Quarry Mine
• Volcano Dungeon
Each dungeon keeps its own visual identity rather than using one identical darkness effect everywhere.
The regular Mines gradually become more threatening as you descend, Skull Cavern and Quarry Mine lean toward a harsher atmosphere, and the Volcano preserves its important lava and authored lighting.


[b]❤️ THE DARK IDEA[/b]
Stardew Valley has plenty of dangerous underground places, but light is rarely something you need to think about.
Dark Descent is designed to change that without turning the game into a complicated survival system.
Descending into a Mine floor and immediately noticing how little you can see.
Finding one surviving lamp in the distance.
Watching your Glow Ring carve a small safe area through the darkness.
Lighting a Torch before pushing deeper into Skull Cavern.
Then reaching a lighter floor and actually feeling the difference.
Small changes to darkness and light - but enough to make descending underground feel like a descent again.



[b]⚙️ REQUIREMENTS[/b]
Required
• SMAPI
Recommended
• Generic Mod Config Menu
No other mods are required.


[b]💡 COMPATIBILITY / GAMEPLAY CLARIFICATION[/b]
Dark Descent is built around Stardew Valley and SMAPI’s normal runtime systems and does not depend on another mod’s content for its core features. Dynamic dungeon darkness, floor variation, Light Failure, player-light protection, dungeon-specific handling, multiplayer behaviour, and configuration are controlled by Dark Descent’s own programmed rules.
The mod does not copy or redistribute another mod’s source code, sprites, maps, lighting assets, dialogue, or other authored content.
Dark Descent uses conservative compatibility behaviour around lighting it cannot confidently identify. Unknown or gameplay-critical light sources are left alone rather than being forcibly disabled.
Compatible additional lighting paths are handled where they can be safely associated with a Dark Descent-managed environmental fixture, while unrelated emissive lighting and visual effects remain untouched.
Generic Mod Config Menu is supported but optional.
Fading Torches is designed to work especially well alongside Dark Descent without being required.

🤖 AI DISCLOSURE
AI assistance was used during development of Dark Descent for planning, coding, debugging, automated testing, lighting analysis, compatibility work, and documentation.
The mod’s concept, design decisions, darkness balance, hands-on gameplay testing, and final approval were done by ACharles.
Dark Descent does not use AI, an LLM, or any generative system while Stardew Valley is running. All darkness, lighting, compatibility, and gameplay behaviour is controlled through predefined rules and programmed game logic.
